summary: search_notes interpolates the search term into the SQL text, so `q` can rewrite the query and read other users' notes or the users table.
delete_note deletes by id alone and ignores owner_id, so any signed-in user can delete any note.
read_attachment joins the requested name onto the attachment folder without checking it, so `../` reaches any file the service can read.
make_archive puts the user's label into a shell command line run with shell=True.
load_prefs unpickles the client-supplied `prefs` cookie, which executes code chosen by the client.
Passwords are stored as unsalted MD5, which is cheap to brute-force and to look up.
